title: Country Sourdough
description: An open, glossy crumb and a crackling crust. A 75% hydration loaf with a touch of wholemeal for flavour.

steps.instruction: Mix both flours with 700 ml of the water until no dry bits remain. Cover and rest (autolyse).
Add the starter, salt and remaining water. Squeeze and fold until the dough feels smooth and strong.
Bulk ferment, doing a set of stretch and folds every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours.
Divide in two, pre-shape into loose rounds and bench rest.
Final shape, place seam-side up in floured bannetons, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Preheat the oven to 250 °C with a Dutch oven inside.
Score and bake covered.
Uncover, drop to 230 °C and bake until deeply golden.
Cool on a rack for at least an hour before slicing. The crumb is still setting.

title: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Nutty brown butter, dark chocolate pools and flaky salt. Crisp edges, chewy middles.

steps.instruction: Brown the butter in a light pan over medium heat, swirling, until it smells nutty and the solids turn amber.
Pour into a bowl and cool until warm, not hot.
Whisk in both sugars, then the eggs and vanilla until glossy.
Fold in the flour, bicarb and salt, then the chocolate.
Chill the dough so the cookies don't spread too far.
Scoop 16 balls onto lined trays and bake at 180 °C.
Sprinkle with flaky salt and leave on the tray to firm up.

title: Classic Butter Croissants
description: A weekend project worth every fold. Three single turns for honeycomb layers.

steps.instruction: Mix the flour, liquids, sugar, yeast, salt and soft butter into a smooth dough. Flatten, wrap and chill overnight.
Pound the laminating butter into a 17 cm square and chill until pliable but cold.
Lock the butter into the dough and give it the first single fold. Chill.
Second single fold. Chill.
Third single fold. Chill.
Roll to 4 mm, cut long triangles and roll them up tightly.
Proof somewhere warm (not above 26 °C) until wobbly and doubled.
Egg wash and bake at 190 °C until deep golden.

title: Lemon Drizzle Loaf
description: A tender, buttery sponge soaked in sharp lemon syrup with a crunchy sugar crust.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour, milk and lemon zest.
Bake until a skewer comes out clean.
Mix the lemon juice with the granulated sugar. Prick the warm cake all over and pour the drizzle on.
Cool completely in the tin so the syrup soaks in.

title: Neapolitan Pizza Dough
description: A slow, cold-fermented dough with leopard-spotted, airy cornicione. Just four ingredients.

steps.instruction: Dissolve the salt in the water, add the flour and yeast and mix to a shaggy dough.
Rest, then knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave at room temperature.
Divide into 4 balls of about 250 g, place in a covered tray and refrigerate for 24 to 48 hours.
Take the balls out of the fridge before baking so they relax.
Stretch by hand, top, and bake in the hottest oven you have.

title: Vanilla Bean Cupcakes
description: Light, moist sponges crowned with a silky vanilla buttercream swirl.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 175 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Rub the soft butter into the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt until sandy.
Whisk the eggs, milk and half the vanilla, then beat into the dry mix until just smooth.
Fill the cases two-thirds full and bake.
Cool completely before icing.
Beat the buttercream butter until pale, add the icing sugar and remaining vanilla, and whip.
Pipe generous swirls on top.

title: Fudgy Brownies
description: That crackly, paper-thin top over a dense, almost molten middle.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 20 cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together over a pan of barely simmering water.
Whisk the eggs and sugar on high until thick and doubled. This makes the crackly top.
Fold in the chocolate, then sift over the flour, cocoa and salt and fold gently.
Bake until the centre just stops wobbling.
Cool fully in the tin before cutting into 16.

title: Brown Sugar Banana Bread
description: The best use for spotty bananas. Moist, caramelly and endlessly snackable.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 170 °C and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Mash the bananas, then whisk in the melted butter, sugar and eggs.
Fold in the flour, bicarb, cinnamon and walnuts until just combined.
Bake until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin, then turn out.

title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, tender stacks for slow Sunday mornings.

steps.instruction: Whisk the dry ingredients in one bowl and the buttermilk, eggs and butter in another.
Combine with a few strokes. Lumps are good. Let the batter rest.
Ladle onto a buttered pan over medium-low heat. Flip when bubbles pop on the surface.
Cook the second side until golden.

title: Spiced Apple Crumble
description: Jammy cinnamon apples under a crisp, oaty, buttery crumble.

ingredients.name: Light brown sugar, for the apples

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 190 °C.
Toss the apples with the brown sugar and cinnamon, then soften in a covered pan.
Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the oats and demerara.
Spread the apples in a dish, scatter the crumble over, and bake until bubbling at the edges.
Rest before serving with custard or ice cream.
